source.title: When Skills Meet Safety: Benchmarking and Characterizing the Adaptive Jailbreak Robustness of Skill-Merged LLMs
source.authors: Yu Ma; Hongli Shi; Jing Li; Xin-Ran Xu; Weiwei Hou

record.tranche_reason: The study intervenes on a weight-space safety direction/subspace and measures refusal-related behavior, rather than using the original harmful-minus-harmless activation-difference method.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports many static and adaptive jailbreak rates for merged models, but those results do not measure whether attacks suppress the refusal direction. They are not linked to a version here. The top-direction Qwen control and the k=1 versus k=8 rank-sensitivity result directly bear on the direction/subspace claims.
record.test_reason: This is a model-merging safety benchmark. It bears on the claim through two results. First, a control that projects Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct's weights off the top direction of the base-minus-abliterated weight difference (k=1), with refusal and capability measured. Second, Table S6, which reports unmerged static ASR for six public uncensored or abliterated Qwen checkpoints. Both are evidence on whether weight edits remove refusal in released models (V2), in a new setting. The difference-in-means activation direction is never computed or ablated, so V1 is not tested directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that static refusal does not predict adaptive jailbreak robustness across six bases, and that the static effect of merging depends on the base. The subspace-overlap signal detects only same-recipe abliteration-style refusal removal, not SFT decensoring or other recipes. SubSafe-Merge removes in-subspace erosion at held capability but cannot fix out-of-subspace erosion or a fragile base. The 'effectively one-dimensional' remark is a limitation note about their estimated weight subspace, not a headline conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The original uses a harmful-minus-harmless activation difference and residual-stream interventions. This paper estimates a weight-space safety subspace from aligned-minus-abliterated model parameters and uses projections.
record.method_sensitivity: In the reported Qwen uncensored-merge setting, safety recovery is reported as insensitive to subspace rank k=1 versus k=8.

fits_no_version.finding: The weight-space task vectors of different public abliteration recipes barely overlap with one another. Overlap with the same-recipe subspace is 0.99 for the same recipe, 0.29–0.32 for two others, and about 0.001–0.003 for the rest. Effective refusal removals occur at every overlap level.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight edits that remove refusal in released models do not share one weight-space direction across recipes. A single-direction weight signature detects only same-recipe abliteration.

fits_no_version.finding: An SFT/DPO-decensored donor is almost orthogonal to S (overlap 0.001) yet removes refusal (static 0.63). Merging it erodes safety in a way that projecting off S cannot undo.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be removed by fine-tuning along weight directions unrelated to the abliteration-derived direction.

fits_no_version.finding: The rank-1 structure of the safety subspace (k=1 and k=8 recover equally; effective rank about 1.01) follows from abliteration being a rank-1 edit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight differences from abliteration are rank-1 per layer by construction, so they cannot test multi-direction accounts.

record.problems: The direct top-direction result is reported only as static ASR and a capability check, with no uncertainty estimate. The projection is a weight-space operation and does not reproduce the original activation-space method. The rank-sensitivity statement gives no separate k=1 numerical result.
record.rows_left_out: Adaptive jailbreak rates and most merge-grid results are not rows here because they do not measure direction suppression or a direction intervention.

untested.parts: The difference-in-means residual-stream direction is never computed. The study does no activation ablation across layers and positions, and no addition of the direction to induce refusal.
There are no abliterations in families other than Qwen; the k=1 control and the Table S6 survey are Qwen2.5-7B only. The study does not report how each public checkpoint's recipe was built.
It does not measure whether GCG, template, PAIR or Crescendo attacks suppress the refusal direction, and does no training against ablation.
There is no activation-space comparison of single versus multi-direction or affine accounts.
Not tested. Overlap differences across abliteration recipes concern weight edits, not transfer of a direction.

missing.what: Unmerged static ASR of six public uncensored or abliterated Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct checkpoints. huihui-ai abliterated-v2: 0.61. Josiefied abliterated-v2: 0.68. Josiefied abliterated-v1: 0.21, near the 0.195 base. jeffmeloy v1.0 and v1.1: 0.67 and 0.42. Orion SFT/DPO: 0.63 (not abliteration).
missing.locator: Table S6; Section 7 and Table S4

record.verdict_notes: The record's challenge to V4 is removed, because the subspace is built from a rank-1 abliteration edit and so cannot show more than one direction. Rows R1–R3 are relinked from V1 to V2, because the intervention is a weight-space edit derived from an abliterated model. The jailbreak and merge-grid results do not measure direction suppression and correctly stay unlinked.

versions.untested_parts: Does not use the original residual-stream difference-in-means direction or ablate it at every layer and position; does not add the direction to induce refusals; tests only a weight-space projection control and static ASR.
Does not test abliteration as a practical weight edit that removes refusal in released models.
Measures attack outcomes on merged models but does not measure whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or train against its ablation.
Tests k=1 versus k=8 for the paper's weight-space safety subspace in one Qwen merge setting; does not compare activation-space affine, cone, or other multi-direction accounts.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
Does not test transfer of the same direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
Does not vary refusal-training method or timing to test their effect on whether a removable direction exists.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Project the base model off the top refusal direction (k=1).
rows.note: The projection substantially raises harmful-compliance ASR, but the reported value is not complete refusal removal.
rows.check: The operation is a weight-space projection off the top singular direction of base-minus-abliterated weights. That is effectively an abliteration-style weight edit, not the difference-in-means activation ablation, so the row belongs under V2 rather than V1. Static ASR rises from 0.20 to 0.64 under a conservative two-judge AND rule. That is substantial but incomplete removal.

source_check.correct: State should be observed: k=1 projection static ASR 0.64 matches or exceeds the full same-recipe public abliteration (huihui-ai abliterated-v2, unmerged static 0.61; uncensored skill at lambda=1.0 is 0.60-0.61 in Table S1). The text calls static 0.42-0.68 'effective refusal-removals'. It gives no refusal rate, and its AND rule is said to slightly under-count.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3 (k=1 control: 0.20 -> 0.64); Table S6 and caption; S5 text ('five of six are effective refusal-removals (static 0.42-0.68)')
source_check.problem: Value is right, but 'partial' conflicts with the study's own reading: 0.64 equals the full abliteration's level, which it calls effective removal.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compare SubSafe-Merge projection using safety-subspace rank k=1 and k=8.
rows.value: Qwen's uncensored merge recovers equally at k=1 and k=8
rows.note: The reported rank comparison finds no additional recovery from k=8 over k=1 in this setting; the text gives no separate numerical values for k=1.
rows.check: The subspace S is estimated from an abliterated model, which is itself a rank-1 edit. Its rank-1 structure (k=1 equals k=8; Table S3 effective rank about 1.01) therefore holds by construction. It cannot speak to whether refusal in activations is affine, a cone, or multi-directional. The row also measures SubSafe-Merge recovery on merges, which is the paper's own method, not refusal mediation.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, k=1 projection and effective public abliterations
relationships.reason: Removal is incomplete under the two-judge AND rule. The k=1 projection reaches 0.64 ASR (R1). Per Table S6, which no row records, the public abliterations huihui-ai v2 and Josiefied v2 reach 0.61 and 0.68 against base 0.195.
relationships.display_finding: Under the two-judge AND rule, single-direction projection achieved 0.64 attack success, while huihui-ai v2 and Josiefied v2 achieved 0.61 and 0.68 versus 0.195 for the base model.

relation.reason: It reports its own refusal-removal results for a weight edit (k=1 projection) and for released abliterated checkpoints, not only its merging method.

tranche.reason: A model-merging benchmark whose results bear on V2: a k=1 weight-projection control (ASR and capability) and a survey of public abliterated checkpoints' unmerged ASR (Table S6). T2 is also defensible for the k=1 control (different direction estimator and measure, same question).

source_check.notes: The text is complete (read in full). S comes from a public same-lineage abliteration; huihui-ai v2 (overlap 0.99) appears to be that source, so R1 re-applies an abliteration-style edit, not a DIM activation ablation. Table S6 is not in the rows: unmerged static ASR huihui-ai v2 0.61, Josiefied v2 0.68, jeffmeloy v1.0 0.67, Josiefied v1 0.21, jeffmeloy v1.1 0.42, Orion SFT/DPO 0.63. Effective removals outside S (Orion, jeffmeloy v1.1) are weight-space only and not a V4 test. The authors_conclusion paraphrase is accurate. The jailbreak templates in S2 are quoted attack prompts, not instructions.
